To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CFAP54 is a novel gene required for ciliary function in mice and is mutated in patients with PCD.
CFAP221 is required for cilia motility and structure and that CFAP54 is required to assemble a central pair projection in mice.
CFAP54 is required to form a functional central pair apparatus and that the absence of CFAP54 leads to a primary ciliary dyskenesia phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the development of the ciliated epithelia.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that control motile cilia function.
the identification of genes involved in cilia and flagellum assembly and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CFAP54 is required in mice for the proper assembly of the central apparatus in motile cilia and for the proper regulation of ciliary motility, and that the gene-trapped mouse model of CFAP54 provides a new animal model for studying the function and assembly of the ciliary central apparatus and for studying ciliary function.
the CFAP54 gene-trap mouse model is a useful tool in understanding the function of the C1d complex and its role in PCD.
CFAP54 is required to assemble the central pair apparatus of motile cilia and is required for proper function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CFAP54 plays a critical role in the assembly of the C1d projections of the central pair of microtubules in mammalian motiile cilia and is required for normal ciliary motility.
the C1D complex is required for ciliogenesis, and its loss causes PCD.
CFAP221 and its homologs are important for proper motility of cilia and flagellum in mice and in Chlamydomona reinhardtii.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CFAP54 is a new gene associated with PCD.
CFAP54 is required in mouse cilia for proper ciliary assembly and function.
we have identified a new gene, CFAP54 (also called CFAP54), that is required for the proper assembly and function in motile cilia and the sperm flagellum.
